adjudication.rationale: The diff shows three separate, hand-copied DB credential fallback implementations with different behavior. In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, if an in-memory credential isn’t found it does `prisma.credential.findUnique({ include: { app: { select: { slug: true }}}})` and only reconstructs `credential` when `credentialFromDB && credentialFromDB.app?.slug` (otherwise it stays undefined and the destination is effectively skipped with no explicit error). In `EventManager.updateCalendarEvents`, the same pattern appears: DB fetch includes `app.slug` and reconstruction is gated on `credentialFromDB.app?.slug`. In `handleCancelBooking`, the DB fallback is `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: credentialId }})` with no `app` include and it accepts any returned credential. So the finding’s claim about duplicated logic and already-divergent rules is directly verifiable from the diff; the part about a “legacy credential with no App row” is plausible but not provable from the diff alone.
